title: New SPHEREx image fits retain the 2025 band of Gaia20cdd and show an unflagged pixel error in one control star
abstract: We test the 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd with new fits to 44 public SPHEREx QR2 and QR3 cutouts. We use the recommended effective point-spread function for both releases and the full science wavelength maps. The 2025 deficit remains with a larger fit area, free source positions and central pixels masked. In one control star, a single pixel with only the SOURCE flag changes its fitted 3.069 um flux from -20 to 922 microJy when removed. The target does not have this core-pixel failure. With a fixed prior band shape, the July 2026 peak depth is 0.305 +/- 0.053 for a linear continuum and 0.259 +/- 0.082 for a quadratic continuum. With the central pixels masked, the quadratic result is 0.222 +/- 0.147. Thus the later visit remains tentative. The new result is an image-level calibration and pixel-influence test, not an independent instrument detection or a water-ice identification. Shared calibration, a small control sample, correlated errors and an unknown stellar reference spectrum limit the interpretation. We provide own image measurements, code, fit results, exact external URLs and hashes, and offline reproduction instructions.
